newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists to return to Japan-claimed isles.
newsitem.headline: HK activists to return to Japan-claimed isles.

text.p: A group of Hong Kong activists said on Tuesday they would make a second attempt to land on disputed islands in the East China Sea to remove all symbols of Japanese claims and reassert China's sovereignty.

The 10 Hong Kong people, who along with Taiwanese activists were repulsed by Japanese patrol ships while trying to land on the archipelago on Monday, have vowed to return to the islands on October 5, a spokesman for the group said.

"Our aim is to land on the Diaoyus and remove the lighthouse built by the Japanese youth group and other symbols, but we will proceed on a peaceful basis," spokesman Au Pak-kuen of Action Committee in Defence of the Diaoyu Islands said by telephone.
Up to 100 activists have applied to join the original group of 10 on the October trip, which would be headed by Democratic Party legislator Tsang Kin-shing, Au said.
Tsang, who returned to Hong Kong on Tuesday, was among the activists repulsed earlier.
The dispute over the uninhabited islands, called the Senkakus in Japan and known to Chinese as the Diaoyus, flared this month when Japanese rightists repaired a lighthouse on one of the islands.
On Monday, 17 Japanese patrol ships backed by a helicopter repulsed a flotilla carrying activists from Taiwan and Hong Kong who were trying to land on the islands to remove the lighthouse.
The group plans to fly on October 5 to Taiwan where, together with Taiwanese activists, it would charter boats to the archipelago, Au said.

Meanwhile, a rusty, 2,800-tonne cargo tanker, the Kien Hwa 2, was headed for the islands with 18 Hong Kong activists, 19 crew and 42 journalists on board. It was scheduled to arrive off the islands early on Thursday.
